chapterName: Empire: The Year of Four Emperors and the Flavians (AD 69-96)

questions.question: What persuaded the Praetorian Guard to desert the last Julio-Claudian emperor in 68?
options: A Senate decree releasing them from their oath
A promise of 30,000 sesterces each in Galba's name
News that the Rhine legions had joined Galba
Galba's promise to double their yearly pay
Threats from the Gallic army camped near Rome
questions.explanation: One of the Guard's own commanders promised each man 30,000 sesterces in Galba's name, roughly ten years' pay. Days later the Senate declared the emperor a public enemy.
questions.sourceQuote: But in Rome the emperor's bodyguard, the Praetorian Guard (*cohortes praetoriae*), deserted him after one of its commanders promised each man 30,000 sesterces in Galba's name, roughly ten years' pay.

questions.question: Which object from the Temple was displayed in Titus and Vespasian's triumph of 71?
options: The altar of burnt offerings
The seven-branched lampstand
The high priest's golden crown
The Temple's great bronze doors
The Ark of the Covenant
questions.explanation: The triumphal parade through Rome displayed the Temple's seven-branched lampstand. A triumph was a formal victory parade.
questions.sourceQuote: In 71 Titus and Vespasian celebrated a triumph (*triumphus*), a victory parade through Rome, displaying the Temple's seven-branched lampstand.

questions.question: According to an ancient biographer, what set Galba apart from other officials when the Gallic revolt began in 68?
options: He alone had served as consul three times
He alone refused the rebel's offer of the throne
He alone was related to the ruling family
He alone sent troops to crush the Gallic rising
He alone did not forward the rebel's letters to the emperor
questions.explanation: An ancient biographer says Galba was the only official who did not pass the rebel's letters on to the emperor. Within weeks his troops proclaimed him emperor.
questions.sourceQuote: According to an ancient biographer, Galba was the only official who did not forward the rebel's letters to the emperor.

questions.question: How did Vespasian's younger son Domitian escape the fighting in Rome in 69?
options: Smuggled out with the Praetorian Guard
Hidden inside a grain cart bound for Ostia
Disguised as a worshipper of the goddess Isis
Dressed as a slave in the Senate's service
Disguised as a priest of Jupiter
questions.explanation: Domitian slipped away disguised as a worshipper of Isis. His uncle, besieged on the Capitoline Hill, was not so lucky and was executed.
questions.sourceQuote: Vespasian's younger son Domitian escaped disguised as a worshipper of the goddess Isis.

questions.question: What was Domitian's approach on the Rhine frontier?
options: Paying yearly tribute to the Germanic tribes
Defence, lining it with roads, forts and watchtowers
Settling defeated Dacians along its banks
Withdrawal of the legions back to Italy
Conquest of all lands as far as the Elbe
questions.explanation: Domitian preferred defence, fortifying the Rhine with roads, forts and watchtowers. Against the Dacians he lost a legion and made a peace critics called disgraceful.
questions.sourceQuote: On the frontiers he preferred defence, lining the Rhine with roads, forts and watchtowers.

questions.question: What change did Domitian make to the denarius, Rome's standard silver coin?
options: He stopped minting it for five years
He replaced it with a gold coin
He had it minted only in Alexandria
He raised its silver content by 12%
He cut its silver content by 12%
questions.explanation: Domitian raised the silver content of the denarius by 12%. He also built or restored around fifty structures.
questions.sourceQuote: He raised the silver content of the denarius, Rome's standard silver coin, by 12%, and built or restored around fifty structures, including a vast palace on the Palatine Hill.

questions.question: What happened to the Gallic rising that started the revolt of 68?
options: The Rhine legions crushed it and its leader killed himself
It marched on Rome and forced the emperor to flee
Galba's troops absorbed it and its leader became consul
The Praetorian Guard crushed it outside Rome
Its leader was executed after Galba took power
questions.explanation: The legions of the Rhine crushed the Gallic rising, and its leader took his own life. The emperor fell anyway, once the Guard deserted him.
questions.sourceQuote: The Gallic rising was crushed by the legions (*legiones*) of the Rhine, and its leader killed himself.

questions.question: What had weakened Jerusalem's defenders before Titus's siege began?
options: An earthquake had brought down most of the city walls
Three rival rebel factions had fought and burned their own food stores
Roman agents had poisoned the city's water supply
The city's leaders had already surrendered to Vespasian
A plague had killed most of the city's defenders
questions.explanation: Three rival rebel factions had fought each other and burned their own food stores. The city was also crowded with refugees and Passover pilgrims.
questions.sourceQuote: He led at least 48,200 soldiers against a city crowded with refugees and Passover pilgrims, where three rival rebel factions had fought each other and burned their own food stores.

questions.question: Which member of Vespasian's family held seven consulships and commanded the Praetorian Guard during his reign?
options: His brother, commander of the city garrison
His grandfather, a former centurion
His younger son Domitian
His son-in-law, a Rhine governor
His elder son Titus
questions.explanation: Titus held seven consulships and commanded the Guard, effectively ruling beside his father. Vespasian made sure power stayed in the family.
questions.sourceQuote: Power stayed in the family: his elder son Titus held seven consulships and commanded the Praetorian Guard, effectively ruling beside him.

questions.question: Which decision by Galba alienated the Praetorian Guard?
options: Disbanding the Guard and replacing it with Spaniards
Appointing Vitellius as the Guard's commander
Moving the Guard to the Rhine frontier
Refusing to pay the reward promised in his name
Ordering the decimation of the Guard
questions.explanation: Galba refused to pay the Guard the reward promised in his name. He also trusted only a small circle of greedy favourites from Spain.
questions.sourceQuote: Galba also refused to pay the Praetorian Guard the reward promised in his name, and he trusted only a small circle of greedy favourites from Spain.
